name: CASETYPE
rule: For 2018-2020, back-fill from EMERGNCY (Yes -> Emergent, No -> Elective) and ELECTSURG. NOT verifiable against data: no year contains both CASETYPE and EMERGNCY, so the mapping is a convention, not a measured equivalence. This is what all_puf_split/build_dataset.py already does to create `case_type`. Urgent cannot be recovered for 2018-2020.

name: ELECTSURG
rule: For 2021+, derive from CASETYPE (Elective -> Yes, otherwise No). Same unverifiable-convention caveat as CASETYPE.

name: EMERGNCY
rule: For 2021+, derive from CASETYPE (Emergent -> Yes, otherwise No). Same unverifiable-convention caveat as CASETYPE.

name: PRHEMOGLOBIN
rule: Approximable from PRHCT, which is present in all 7 years: PRHEMOGLOBIN = 0.344 * PRHCT -0.56, fitted on 169,354 2023 pairs: R2 = 0.74, median absolute error 0.33, 90th percentile 0.83. Good enough to impute a level, not to reproduce the exact value.

name: HEMO
rule: See PRHEMO_A1C: HEMO is the 2021-2022 name for the same measurement. HEMO in 2022 has median 5.9 (5th-95th pct 5.0-8.9) and PRHEMO_A1C in 2023 has median 5.8 (4.9-8.6) -- the same HbA1c% scale; PRHEMOGLOBIN sits at median 13.2 (9.3-15.9), a different measurement entirely. So HEMO is HbA1c, not haemoglobin

name: PRHEMO_A1C
rule: For 2021-2022, back-fill from HEMO. VERIFIED by value distribution rather than assumed: HEMO in 2022 has median 5.9 (5th-95th pct 5.0-8.9) and PRHEMO_A1C in 2023 has median 5.8 (4.9-8.6) -- the same HbA1c% scale; PRHEMOGLOBIN sits at median 13.2 (9.3-15.9), a different measurement entirely. So HEMO is HbA1c, not haemoglobin. This is what all_puf_split/build_dataset.py already does to create `hba1c`.
